papers.title: 3D Bioprinting of Developmentally Inspired Templates for Whole Bone Organ Engineering
papers.abstract: The ability to print defined patterns of cells and extracellular-matrix components in three dimensions has enabled the engineering of simple biological tissues; however, bioprinting functional solid organs is beyond the capabilities of current biofabrication technologies. An alternative approach would be to bioprint the developmental precursor to an adult organ, using this engineered rudiment as a template for subsequent organogenesis in vivo. This study demonstrates that developmentally inspired hypertrophic cartilage templates can be engineered in vitro using stem cells within a supporting gamma-irradiated alginate bioink incorporating Arg-Gly-Asp adhesion peptides. Furthermore, these soft tissue templates can be reinforced with a network of printed polycaprolactone fibers, resulting in a ≈350 fold increase in construct compressive modulus providing the necessary stiffness to implant such immature cartilaginous rudiments into load bearing locations. As a proof-of-principal, multiple-tool biofabrication is used to engineer a mechanically reinforced cartilaginous template mimicking the geometry of a vertebral body, which in vivo supported the development of a vascularized bone organ containing trabecular-like endochondral bone with a supporting marrow structure. Such developmental engineering approaches could be applied to the biofabrication of other solid organs by bioprinting precursors that have the capacity to mature into their adult counterparts over time in vivo.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇论文是关于3D生物打印骨器官工程的，完全不涉及AI或机器学习，与AI辅助生物打印方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate any AI, machine learning, or autonomous decision-making into the bioprinting workflow.

summary_zh.motivation: 打印功能性固体器官超出当前技术能力，探索打印发育前体作为体内器官发生的模板。
summary_zh.method: 使用干细胞和γ辐照海藻酸盐生物墨水打印肥大软骨模板，并用PCL纤维增强机械性能。
summary_zh.result: 构建的机械增强软骨模板在体内支持血管化骨器官形成，包括小梁骨和骨髓结构。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外力学测试和体内植入大鼠模型验证模板的成骨能力。

summary_en.motivation: Current biofabrication cannot print functional solid organs, prompting an alternative approach using bioprinted developmental precursors as templates for in vivo organogenesis.
summary_en.method: Hypertrophic cartilage templates were bioprinted using stem cells in an alginate bioink and reinforced with printed polycaprolactone fibers to achieve mechanical stiffness.
summary_en.result: The reinforced cartilaginous templates, mimicking vertebral body geometry, supported vascularized bone organ development with trabecular bone and marrow in vivo.
summary_en.validation: In vitro mechanical testing confirmed a 350-fold increase in compressive modulus, and in vivo implantation in rats demonstrated endochondral bone formation.
